data.title: Fluticasone propionate + Mupirocin cream
data.summary: IV Topical corticosteroids · Combination: medium-potency fluorinated steroid (fluticasone 0.05%, US class 5) + mupirocin 2%
data.body:
_Topicals · IV Topical corticosteroids_

**Class:** Combination: medium-potency fluorinated steroid (fluticasone 0.05%, US class 5) + mupirocin 2%

## Mechanism of action
- Fluticasone: potent glucocorticoid receptor agonist with rapid hepatic inactivation (low systemic effect)
- Mupirocin: isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase inhibitor — kills S. aureus and Streptococcus that colonise and worsen eczema

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Secondarily infected (impetiginised) eczema and dermatitis — short term
- Infected insect bite reactions, infected lichen simplex

## Dose & formulations
- Twice daily for 7–10 days, then switch to plain steroid

## Adverse effects
- Steroid side effects with misuse; mupirocin resistance with long use; burning

## Contraindications
- Primary bacterial, fungal or viral infections without dermatitis; rosacea, acne
- Not for long-term use

## Pregnancy & lactation
Acceptable on limited areas.

## Viva points
- Rational combination only for short-term infected eczema
- Fluticasone is safe in children (approved from 3 months) as plain cream

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.45 and ch.41; Khopkar ch.22. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
